Subject: Competitive bake-off recap + next steps — Redwood vs competitors (NovaHealth)

Hi Priya / Daniel,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the detailed walkthrough of NovaHealth's inference needs. Below is a concise recap from our call, the decision criteria you highlighted, and proposed next steps for the bake-off. Please flag any corrections.

Recap of pain points & goals
- High per-token cost and unpredictable unit economics on peak days (billing variability across teams).
- Latency SLOs: 95th pct < 180ms for 1-2k qps traffic on clinical assistants.
- Data controls: VPC+KMS for PHI-sensitive prompts and audit logs for compliance.
- Need model QA baseline to ensure clinical hallucinations are below current threshold.

Decision criteria (ranked)
1) Latency & tail latency (95/99th) across typical sequence lengths
2) Cost per 1k tokens at target throughput
3) Model quality on NovaHealth prompts / safety regression risk
4) Operational controls (VPC, KMS, audit logs)
5) On-prem / Private deployment option (if required for regulated workflows)

Competitive landscape covered on call
- Redwood Inference (us): unified runtime with batching, KV caching, quantization profiles and smart routing between hosted/dedicated/private.
- Competitor A (vendor you mentioned): good latency in isolated tests but lacked prefix caching and had limited KV cache visibility.
- Competitor B: stronger for embeddings cost but higher tail latency on long sequences.

Proposed bake-off tests (we recommend running these in parallel across vendors)
1) Latency sweep: 3 sequence lengths (short: 32 tokens, mid: 256, long: 1024) at 100, 500, 2k qps for 30-minute windows — collect p50/p95/p99 and GPU utilization.
2) Regression QA set: run our 250-case clinical prompt set against each model / deployment to compare hallucination / factuality metrics.
3) Cost simulation: end-to-end simulated traffic for a 24-hour peak period to estimate unit cost and autoscaling behavior.

Attachments (attached): redwood_bakeoff_plan.xlsx (test plan), latency_benchmarks.pdf (recent public benchmarks), nova_test_dataset.csv (sample QA prompts)

Next steps
- We'll upload the formal test plan and baseline scripts to your shared Drive folder by EOD today.
- Can you confirm tests owners and preferred dates for the runs? We suggest starting the latency sweep on Monday 7/20.
- Rishi will follow up on SOW and procurement asks (cc'd).

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

Best,

Perfect — thanks Priya. Quick responses inline and updated plan attached.

1) Hallucination / safety metrics: we'll run the 250-case regression set and report per-case error tags (hallucination, omission, safety flag). We'll provide a short evaluation pipeline (Python scripts + instructions) that outputs aggregate precision/recall-like metrics for regression detection.
2) Cold-start burst: included — plan now specifies a 5-minute cold-start burst (50 short requests/sec) followed by steady-state periods. We'll capture startup latency and queueing behavior.
3) Pricing: attached is a preliminary pricing sheet with hosted tiers and a Dedicated 4-GPU monthly commitment estimate (line-item costs, expected savings with batching and prefix caching). Final numbers will depend on actual run utilization; this is to help procurement budget.

Attachments: redwood_bakeoff_plan.xlsx; latency_benchmarks.pdf; nova_test_dataset.csv

Proposed schedule
- Fri 7/17: Redwood uploads Drive folder + run scripts (we'll share permissions to your team).
- Mon 7/20 AM: Latency sweep (short/mid/long + cold-start burst).
- Mon 7/20 PM: Start regression QA run (overnight for aggregate metrics).
- Tue 7/21: Cost simulation and debrief with results.

If that looks good I'll mark the run owners and trigger the HubSpot tasks.

Cheers,
Aditya
